name: Simple Seafood Chowder with Potatoes and Bread

components.name: Seafood Chowder

ingredients.name: Mixed raw fish (salmon, haddock, smoked haddock)

steps: Heat 15 ml oil in a deep pot and sauté diced bacon and onion until bacon is cooked and onion softens.
Add 15 g flour and stir for 2 minutes to coat the vegetables; slowly add 600 ml fish stock.
Put in the diced potatoes and simmer until they are almost tender, around 10-12 minutes.
Add milk, mace, cayenne and a little of the measured salt; lower the heat to avoid boiling the dairy.
Add raw mixed fish and gently poach until cooked through. Stir in the raw shucked shellfish and 60 ml single cream and gently simmer until all seafood is fully cooked.

components.name: Wholegrain Bread
steps: Sprinkle parsley and portion chowder with 40 g bread per serving. Chill and consume early in the week.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.
Source includes bacon, salmon, smoked haddock, precooked mixed shellfish and potatoes; UNHANGRY uses 280 g raw shellfish, adjusting weight and cooking time, and adds 160 g bread as a complete meal.
Storing & reheating: Published recipe advises refrigerated leftovers for up to 2 days. Do not freeze assembled cream, fish and potatoes if texture matters.
Freezer: milk and fish chowder changes texture
Allergens: Fish, Shellfish / molluscs, Dairy, Wheat / gluten, CONTAINS PORK / NON-HALAL

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish to 63°C, shrimp and shellfish until opaque and firm (mussels must open), and reheat to at least 74°C.

foodSafety: Refrigerate perishables promptly in shallow containers: within 2 hours after cooking, or within 1 hour if the air temperature is above 32 C.
Store at 4 C or colder. General cooked-leftover limit: 3-4 days; for delicate seafood recipes follow any shorter specific limit above.
Freeze later-week portions promptly, if this recipe is flagged freezer-suitable; thaw in refrigerator, not on a kitchen counter.
For fish, target a safe cooked internal temperature of 63 C; shrimp and shellfish should be cooked until opaque / firm, and mussels must open during cooking.
Reheat leftovers thoroughly to 74 C, avoiding repeated reheating and cooling cycles.
Cooked rice requires rapid chilling, appropriate cold storage and thorough reheating. Rice left warm for a prolonged period is not made safe by reheating.
Shellfish, fish, soy, dairy, wheat, egg, nuts and pork vary by recipe; verify allergens and dietary restrictions before importing.
